channel.title: The Cypherpunk Handbook - Articles
channel.description: Latest articles and updates from the Cypherpunk Handbook.

item.title: The C language's biggest problem: evidence of its insecurity
item.description: C permits unchecked pointer arithmetic, out-of-bounds access, use after free, and other forms of undefined behavior. Vendor data from Microsoft, Google, and Android shows why memory safety remains a dominant security problem in large C and C++ codebases.

item.title: Why OpenBSD stands alone
item.description: OpenBSD integrates secure defaults, source auditing, exploit mitigations, privilege-separated daemons, and small base-system implementations. This article explains why that coherent architecture remains superior to hardened Linux, Windows, macOS, mobile systems, and competing BSD designs.

item.title: From a strict security perspective, Qubes OS is not reliable
item.description: This critique evaluates Qubes OS through Xen, dom0, device domains, hardware trust, recovery, and total trusted computing base. It recognizes the value of compartmentalization while explaining where shared hardware and privileged infrastructure limit that model.

item.title: Self-hosting SearXNG on OpenBSD over a Tor onion service
item.description: This guide shows how to self-host SearXNG on OpenBSD and expose it through a Tor onion service while keeping privileges separated and permissions minimal.

item.title: Security terms in operating systems
item.description: This glossary defines security terms you will repeatedly encounter in OS hardening, exploit mitigation, identity control, trusted boot, virtualization, and network defense. Each entry is short, practical, and paired with an example so the concept is easy to apply in real systems.

item.title: Why I stopped using Linux
item.description: After thirteen years with Linux, I left because its security model, integration burden, operational complexity, and project culture no longer met my requirements. This article explains that decision and identifies the alternatives I consider superior.
